title: Idempotent delta streaming with deterministic replay tokens and graceful retry
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: clients and SDKs intermittently lose connectivity while ingesting server-sent incremental outputs (text tokens, structured deltas, and function-call fragments). Partial application of duplicated or missing deltas leads to duplicated function calls, corrupted structured outputs, or state drift in downstream consumers. Current stream variants lack a deterministic, compact handshake token that lets a client reconnect and request exactly the missing work without forcing a full snapshot or brittle sequence-number assumptions.

Goal: implement an idempotent delta streaming flow that: (1) emits compact deterministic replay tokens (tokenflow) with provenance metadata for each stable checkpoint, (2) verifies chunk integrity on reconnect using a lightweight checksum, (3) preserves semantic boundaries for function/tool call frames and structured outputs, and (4) defines a graceful downgrade path to non-streaming or snapshot resend for older clients. The solution must be backward-compatible with older SDKs via explicit feature negotiation and opt-in rollout.

Scope: server-side token generator and verifier, protocol header for feature negotiation, client reconnect handler changes in JS/Python SDKs, end-to-end tests, and gradual rollout plan (canary + metrics). Not in scope: changing token storage semantics for Dedicated clusters (follow-up ticket).
acceptance_criteria: 1) Server produces deterministic replay tokens after each stable checkpoint: token contains stable_offset, window_id, CRC32 checksum, and protocol_version string
2) Client can reconnect and send the last token; server responds with a compact delta set (only missing items) or a full snapshot if delta set cannot be reconstructed
3) Function-call and structured output boundaries are never split across segments in a way that breaks parser invariants; SDKs can rehydrate the output deterministically
4) Feature negotiation header (X-Redwood-Stream-Proto) allows old clients to fall back to current behavior; no silent protocol breaks
5) End-to-end test suite covers mid-stream disconnects at random offsets and verifies idempotency of replays
6) Metrics emitted: reconnect_rate_by_client_version, replay_delta_size_distribution, resume_failure_rate, duplicated_function_call_rate
7) Rollout: canary 5% with zero increase in duplicated_function_call_rate (target < 0.01%) before 100% ramp
implementation_plan: Design: finalize token layout and header semantics (this ticket)
Server: implement token creation at checkpoint boundary in stream runtime; attach token to 'checkpoint' events
Server: implement compact delta responder that takes a client token and returns missing delta list or a snapshot fallback
SDKs: add reconnect handshake that sends last_token in the initial resume request; verify server response and apply deltas idempotently
Compatibility: add X-Redwood-Stream-Proto header; support v1 (current) and v0 (legacy) behaviors
Tests: unit tests for token generator/verifier, integration tests for checksum mismatch paths, chaos tests for flapping connections
Docs: write protocol spec for external SDK authors and customers; include migration guide
Rollout: create canary config in infra with 5% traffic and observability dashboards
testing_plan: Unit: token assembly and parsing round-trip (including CRC mismatch)
Integration: run SDK JS + Python E2E where we simulate disconnect at 20ms, 200ms, and 2s after stream start
Chaos: scripted flaps and out-of-order retransmits to ensure idempotent application
Property tests: random delta sequences applied twice yield same final state
Performance: measure added latency at checkpoint emission (target < 0.5ms median per request)
Canary monitors: compare duplicated_function_call_rate and resume_failure_rate vs baseline
comments: 2025-11-10 - Asha Patel: Triage note. Spike planned to evaluate token formats (sequence-range vs offset+window). Assigned to Miguel.

2025-11-12 - Miguel Sanchez: Spike complete. Offset+window approach with CRC proved smallest and easiest to verify in runtime. Prototype generator in runtime/stream/checkpoint.go. Found edge case when KV-cache gets trimmed mid-window — we must include a tombstone indicator in the token.

2025-11-13 - Priya Nair (Design): Reviewed prototype. Request: explicit semantic_boundary flag to prevent splitting function_call frames across delta sets. Also asked for clear fallback when CRC mismatch occurs.

2025-11-14 - Miguel Sanchez: Implemented 'token.provenance' fields: stable_offset, window_id, crc32, semantic_boundary=true/false. Added server-side fallback that returns 'full_snapshot' if either token is stale or provenance indicates missing origins.

2025-11-15 - QA (Luca): Created initial E2E harness and observed a rare case where duplicate function calls appear when the client applied a delta set then received an overlapping delta on reconnect; root cause: SDK applied optimistic partial frames before verifying checkpoint. Action: SDK must buffer until checkpoint verification completes.

2025-11-16 - Miguel Sanchez: SDK change committed to python-sdk (PR linked). It buffers partial function_call frames until finalizing checkpoint verification. Also added exponential jittered backoff for resume attempts (base=200ms, cap=5s).
2025-11-17 - Priya Nair: Design review approved pending metrics and canary plan. Please ensure metric labels expose client_version and protocol_version.
2025-11-18 - Release Engineering (Jin): Scheduled canary for 2025-11-25 on runtime-1.24. Need deployment plan for Dedicated clusters (follow-up ticket requested).
